issues.body: `LABEL_WRITE_PATTERNS` recognizes a `/labels` API call only when it contains an explicit `-X/--method POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE`. GitHub CLI's `gh api` automatically switches from GET to POST when fields are supplied, so a label write such as `gh api repos/$R/issues/$N/labels -f 'labels[]=needs:user'` is mutating but is not classified as a label-writing step. A foreign PAT in that step therefore escapes R1 entirely, contradicting the advertised invariant that every label-writing step carries bot identity. The positive fixtures cover `gh pr edit`, script indirection, and output laundering, but not either explicit-method or implicit-method REST writes.
issues.fix_hint: Detect mutating `gh api` label endpoints when request fields/input imply the CLI's default POST (including `-f`, `-F`, `--raw-field`, `--field`, and `--input` as applicable), while continuing to exclude genuine GET requests. Add positive self-test fixtures for both explicit-method and implicit-default-POST `/labels` writes, plus a negative GET fixture, so this branch cannot pass vacuously.
issues.title: Default-POST `gh api` label writes bypass the identity guard

verdict.summary: The guard and its supplied self-test pass, but the label-write classifier does not cover a standard mutating `gh api` form. Because the workflow claims to enforce bot identity on every label-writing step, this false negative leaves the central security invariant bypassable and is not exercised by the fixtures.
